source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part III, Ch. 15 (Framing the Constitution).

sections.heading: 1. The Constituent Assembly
points: After Independence, the **Constituent Assembly** framed India's Constitution (December 1946 – 1949).
The Assembly was **indirectly elected** (by the provincial assemblies); dominated by the **Congress** but broadly representative.
Key figures: **Dr Rajendra Prasad (President)**, **Dr B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman, Drafting Committee)**, **Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, Rajaji, K.M. Munshi**.

sections.heading: 2. The Vision and Debates
points: The **Objectives Resolution (Nehru, 1946)** laid out the ideals — sovereignty, justice, liberty, equality, fraternity — later reflected in the **Preamble**.
Debates on: **the rights of minorities, language, the powers of the Centre vs states, and reservations**.
The Assembly debated whether India should have a **strong Centre** — settled in favour of a strong Centre (given Partition and unity concerns).

sections.heading: 3. Key Issues Debated
points: **Language:** Hindi (in Devanagari) was made the official language, with English continued for a period — a **compromise** after intense debate.
**The rights of the depressed classes:** abolition of untouchability and **reservations for SCs/STs** (championed by Ambedkar).
**Federalism:** division of powers, but with a strong Union to preserve unity.
The role of the state in social and economic reform (Directive Principles).

sections.heading: 4. Adoption
points: The Constitution was **adopted on 26 November 1949** and came into force on **26 January 1950**.
It sought to balance **unity, democracy, social justice, and diversity**.
The debates (recorded in the Constituent Assembly Debates) are a rich source for the making of modern India.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Constituent Assembly (1946–49); indirectly elected; Congress-dominated but representative.
Rajendra Prasad = President; Ambedkar = Chairman of Drafting Committee.
Objectives Resolution (Nehru, 1946) → basis of the Preamble.
Language compromise: Hindi (official) + English continued.
Adopted 26 Nov 1949; enforced 26 Jan 1950.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Objectives Resolution** was moved by **Nehru (1946)** — basis of the Preamble.
**Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee**; **Rajendra Prasad** was Assembly President.
The **language question** was settled by compromise (Hindi + English continued).
The Constitution was **adopted 26 Nov 1949**, in force **26 Jan 1950**.
